claim: Convergent extension dramatically elongates the hindbrain and spinal cord of vertebrates, but not the midbrain and forebrain.

claim: Disruption of planar cell polarity (PCP) genes results in failure of neural tube closure in posterior regions of the neural ectoderm, but not anterior.
source: Accordingly, disruption of genetic regulators of convergent extension such as the planar cell polarity (PCP) genes results in failure of neural tube closure in posterior regions of the neural ectoderm, but not anterior (Kibar et al., 2001; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kibar et al., 2001 and Wang et al., 2006

claim: Shroom3 is implicated in apical constriction.
source: Conversely, the shroom3 gene is implicated in apical constriction, a distinct cell behavior that drives epithelial sheet bending, and disruption of shroom3 elicits highly penetrant defects in anterior neural tube closure, but only weakly penetrant defects in the posterior (Haigo et al., 2003; Hildebrand and Soriano, 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haigo et al., 2003 and Hildebrand and Soriano, 1999

claim: Disruption of shroom3 elicits highly penetrant defects in anterior neural tube closure, but only weakly penetrant defects in the posterior.
source: Conversely, the shroom3 gene is implicated in apical constriction, a distinct cell behavior that drives epithelial sheet bending, and disruption of shroom3 elicits highly penetrant defects in anterior neural tube closure, but only weakly penetrant defects in the posterior (Haigo et al., 2003; Hildebrand and Soriano, 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haigo et al., 2003 and Hildebrand and Soriano, 1999

claim: Apical constriction is driven by actomyosin contraction.
source: While apical constriction is driven by actomyosin contraction, the precise site of actomyosin action during this process is unclear and constitutes a long-term problem in the field (Martin and Goldstein, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Martin and Goldstein, 2014

claim: Analysis of apical constriction during gastrulation in Drosophila and Caenorhabditis elegans has shown integration of discrete junctional and medio-apical ('medial') populations of actomyosin.

claim: Pulsed medial actomyosin-based contractions occur during neural tube closure in frog and chick embryos.

evidence: Supported by citations to Brown and García-García, 2018; Christodoulou and Skourides, 2015; Suzuki et al., 2017

claim: Shroom3 is both necessary and sufficient to drive apical constriction in a variety of cell types, including the closing neural tube.
